findings.reason: without saying what `finding_unit` returns for a multi-section finding (or that the delivery path must become multi-valued), the node either silently under-blocks to one section or invents a shape the plan does not authorise, and §13's own arm "each refuse exactly the sections their text names" would pass only on the grouping function while the delivery path stays wrong.
findings.text: §13 states a source-anchored finding "resolves to the sections its text names (§N or sN), each of which it blocks", and says "The delivery of findings to sections that already uses `_anchor_unit` gains the same correction"; that delivery path is `finding_unit` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2424`), whose return type is a single `str` and which the response writer stores as `response["section"] = finding_unit(record, finding_id)` at `plan_review.py:2058`, so a finding naming two sections cannot be recorded as blocking both and a node implementing this hits an interface that cannot carry the stated rule
